sources.title: Data sources
sources.esg: ESG scores: MSCI ESG Research data (via iShares/BlackRock issuer fact sheets) for covered funds, otherwise Seedow's proprietary model or Yahoo — the source and date are stored per asset (esg_score_source, esg_data_asof). Provider connection is rolling out fund by fund.
sources.carbon: Carbon intensity (gCO₂e/€ invested): a per-asset field with source and date is in place, but no emissions provider is connected yet — real coverage is currently 0%, which the methodology page shows honestly.
sources.sfdr: SFDR classification: issuer prospectuses (iShares, Lyxor, Amundi)
sources.prices: Prices and volatilities: Yahoo Finance, 5-year historical series, covariances recalculated weekly

esg_composite.title: Composite ESG score, weighted by your causes
esg_composite.desc_1: The ESG score ranges from 0 to 100.
esg_composite.desc_2: Instead of a fixed 40/40/20 average, the E, S, and G pillars are reweighted based on the causes you activate in your preferences. The score thus reflects what really matters to you.
esg_composite.pillar_e: Environment (E) — scope 1-2 CO₂ emissions (scope 3 when the issuer discloses it), carbon intensity, water, waste, renewables exposure.
esg_composite.pillar_s: Social (S) — human rights, working conditions, gender equality, product safety, community relations.
esg_composite.pillar_g: Governance (G) — board independence, executive compensation, tax ethics, transparency, anti-corruption.
esg_composite.fallback_note: When a pillar is not published for an asset, we automatically fall back on the global ESG score (documented fallback).
esg_composite.mapping_e: Climate, Biodiversity, Circular economy → boost the E pillar
esg_composite.mapping_s: Human rights, Gender equality → boost the S pillar
esg_composite.mapping_sg: Ethical tech → boost the S and G pillars
esg_composite.mapping_note: Without an active cause, we revert to the neutral 40/40/20 weighting. The more causes you activate related to a pillar, the more its weight in the composite score increases.
esg_composite.portfolio_desc: It is the weighted average of the composite score of each line by its weight. A default ESG floor of 70 is imposed on the optimizer; if it finds no feasible solution, the floor is relaxed and an esg_floor_relaxed flag is raised for transparency.
esg_composite.warning: An ESG rating remains an estimation dependent on the quality of published data. Each asset stores the score source (esg_score_source) for traceability.

carbon.title: Carbon footprint: heuristic + real
carbon.desc: Two indicators deliberately coexist while real data coverage reaches 100% of the portfolio:
carbon.avoided: Avoided CO₂ (heuristic) — indicative estimation derived from the composite ESG score. Practical for comparing two portfolios, not a regulatory figure.
carbon.intensity: Real carbon intensity — weighted average of gCO₂e/€ invested/year on the portion of the portfolio actually covered by a provider (carbon_intensity_* fields with source and update date). A coverage indicator is displayed in the methodology page.
carbon.coverage_title: Low coverage? Heres what to do
carbon.coverage_low: < 30% — rely on avoided CO₂ heuristic, real intensity is not representative.
carbon.coverage_medium: 30–70% — indicative reading, to be cross-referenced with composite ESG.
carbon.coverage_high: ≥ 70% — reliable figure, usable for internal reporting.

optimization.title: Constrained Markowitz optimization
optimization.desc: Maximization of mean-variance utility with constraints: sum of weights = 1, weights ≥ 0, floor per asset, ceiling per asset and class, risk budget (target volatility), composite ESG floor. Expected returns are tilted upstream according to your causes (single-tilt pre-optimization) — no double-tilt at the exit to avoid biasing the efficient frontier.

version.title: Engine version
version.desc: Methodology v1.1 · E/S/G pillars weighted by causes, real carbon intensity, source traceability. Revised quarterly.

methodologie.title: Methodology
methodologie.meta_desc: Portfolio construction pipeline: exclusions, best-in-class, constrained Markowitz optimization, conviction tilts.
methodologie.intro: Five transparent and reproducible steps. Adjust the parameters at the bottom of the page to see the portfolio recomposed live.
methodologie.simulator_desc: Any modification below recalculates the allocation according to the complete pipeline.
methodologie.esg_floor_relaxed_desc: With these constraints, the optimizer could not find a portfolio satisfying the minimum ESG score of 70/100. The floor was lifted to produce a viable allocation. The score shown below is the actual score obtained.
methodologie.metric_sharpe_hint: Net of fees and risk-free rate
methodologie.impact_waci_none: Real carbon intensity unavailable for this selection — connection in progress.
methodologie.impact_note: WACI = weighted average carbon intensity in tCO₂e per $M of revenue (SFDR PAI indicator, MSCI data via issuer fact sheets). The Seedow reference is a composite mix aligned with the portfolio's equity/bond/real/cash allocation (MSCI ACWI for equities, Bloomberg Global Aggregate for bonds, Scope 1+2, June 2026). It avoids comparing a bond portfolio to an equity index. The rest of the portfolio uses proprietary scoring, connection in progress.
methodologie.no_positions: No positions retained with these constraints.

stages.2_desc: ~40 multi-class assets: equities, green bonds, thematics, REITs, money market.
stages.3_desc: Hard sector exclusions, then best-in-class ESG (top 50% per class — median).
stages.4_desc: Linear adjustment of expected returns according to your causes (≤ +1.5% per cause). No full Black-Litterman.
stages.5_desc: Constrained Markowitz: max return / variance, bounds per class and composite ESG floor weighted E/S/G according to your causes.

methodologie.reading_p1: You pick what matters to you (causes), what you refuse (exclusions), how much risk you accept and for how long. We instantly rebuild a concrete portfolio that fits your choices.
methodologie.reading_p2: The figures on the right summarise what this portfolio should return, its risk level, fees and footprint. Hover the « ? » for a plain-language explanation of each term.

glossary.markowitz: Markowitz: a mathematical recipe that combines assets to target the best possible return for a given level of risk.
glossary.best_in_class: Best-in-class: we only keep the top half of each category on ESG criteria.
glossary.ter: TER: annual fees taken from a fund (e.g. 0.20% = €2 per year for €1,000 invested).
glossary.esg_acro: ESG: Environment, Social, Governance — the three pillars of responsible finance.

tips.stage_1: Your personal preferences. The raw material for everything else.
tips.stage_2: The toolkit: the list of financial products we can pick from (equities, bonds, real estate…).
tips.stage_3: First we remove what you refuse (e.g. weapons), then we only keep the top performers of each category on ESG criteria.
tips.stage_4: We slightly increase the expected weight of assets aligned with your priority causes. A nudge, not a sledgehammer.
tips.stage_5: A mathematical calculation that combines the remaining assets to target the best possible return at the risk level you chose.
tips.causes: The topics your money should push forward (climate, biodiversity…). The higher the intensity, the more the portfolio leans towards these topics.
tips.exclusions: The sectors you refuse to finance. Ticked = strictly excluded from the portfolio.
tips.risk: How much the portfolio value can move from one year to the next. The higher, the more it can rise… and fall.
tips.horizon: How long you plan to leave this money invested. The longer, the more variation we can accept.
tips.return: What the portfolio could return on average each year, before fees and taxes. Not a guarantee.
tips.volatility: The typical size of annual swings. Volatility 10% ≈ portfolio may swing about ±10% over a year.
tips.sharpe: Return obtained per unit of risk taken. The higher, the better risk is rewarded. Above 1 is very good.
tips.esg: Score out of 100 summarising the environmental, social and governance quality of the portfolio. Higher = stronger impact.
tips.fees: Average annual cost of the products held, automatically deducted from performance. Lower is better.
tips.co2: Estimated tonnes of CO₂ avoided each year for €10,000 invested, compared to a classic portfolio.
tips.carbon_intensity: Grams of CO₂ emitted each year for every euro invested. Real data when the provider publishes it, otherwise unavailable.
tips.carbon_coverage: Share of the portfolio for which we have the official carbon data. The higher, the more reliable the figure.
tips.allocation: The precise list of products selected and the weight of each one in your portfolio.
tips.breakdown: How money is split between major asset families (equities, bonds, real estate…). Good diversification limits surprises.

methodologie.carbon_coverage_advice_none: No portfolio asset publishes official carbon intensity yet. The figure shown remains indicative.
methodologie.carbon_coverage_advice_low: Too few assets publish their carbon footprint. Take the figure with caution.
methodologie.carbon_coverage_advice_mid: Partial coverage: the figure is extrapolated from the documented part of the portfolio.
methodologie.carbon_coverage_advice_high: Good coverage: the figure is reliable for indicative reporting.
methodologie.proprietary_notice_body: Part of the investment universe is rated using Seedow's proprietary rating (v1), not MSCI. It applies while third-party data feeds are being connected — the exact source (MSCI, Seedow, or Yahoo Finance) is shown on every asset sheet.
methodologie.details_esg_toggle: Show ESG score detail (sources, grid, limits)
methodologie.source_link_label: Where does this number come from?

equity.title: Stock fund (ETF)
equity.desc: a basket bundling hundreds of companies. You don't pick one: you invest in the whole set at once, which spreads the risk.

thematic.title: Thematic fund
thematic.desc: a basket of companies grouped around one theme (e.g. renewable energy). More focused, so more concentrated and more sensitive to that theme's ups and downs.

bond.title: Bond
bond.desc: you lend money to a government or company, which pays you interest and repays you at maturity. Usually steadier than a stock.

comparatif_panel.why_gap_q: Why does my Seedow portfolio differ from the {{bench}} on impact and performance? Explain it simply.
comparatif_panel.projection_disclaimer: Illustrative projection based on a constant annual return assumption — not a guarantee or an actual performance track record. Markets vary; your real result may differ significantly.
comparatif_panel.carbon_intensity_hint: Computed from real issuer data (WACI), not an estimate.
comparatif_panel.methodology_body: The benchmark uses the average characteristics of a MSCI World UCITS ETF (IWDA / EUNL): long-term annualized performance of 7.2% (net dividends), volatility 15.5%, TER 0.20%, MSCI ESG score ~52, carbon intensity 165 gCO₂e per euro invested.
comparatif_panel.benchmark_no_data_body: Seedow only shows verified figures. This benchmark has no real data loaded yet in our database — we never invent a value instead.
comparatif_panel.reward_risk_note: Expected return ÷ volatility. Higher = better paid for the risk taken.
comparatif_panel.risk_adjusted_body: Comparing a multi-asset portfolio to a 100% equity index without adjusting for risk is meaningless: you always lose in a bull market and always win in a bear one. Below, {{bench}} is scaled down to your volatility ({{vol}}%) — the remaining capital earns nothing.
comparatif_panel.price_cost: At comparable risk, your portfolio projects {{delta}} € LESS than {{bench}} over 10 years, on {{capital}} € invested. That is the cost of your exclusions and impact constraints — we do not hide it.
comparatif_panel.price_gain: At comparable risk, your portfolio projects {{delta}} € MORE than {{bench}} over 10 years, on {{capital}} € invested.
comparatif_panel.downside_body: A 30% drop on {{bench}} would translate, proportionally to volatility, into roughly {{drop}}% on your portfolio. What would be left of {{capital}} €:
comparatif_panel.downside_note: Proportional estimate based on volatilities, not a forecast. A less volatile portfolio usually falls less — it does not never fall.
comparatif_panel.window_note: Expected returns estimated on the real price history available (rolling 2-year window), with capped James-Stein shrinkage anchored per asset class. A short window overstates recently strong asset classes.

reglages_inline.auto_recalc_note: Any change triggers an automatic recalculation of your portfolio through the full pipeline (exclusions → best-in-class → constrained Markowitz optimization → conviction tilts).
reglages_inline.cron_empty: No logged executions yet. Force a refresh above to start tracking.
reglages_inline.pipeline_body: Six traceable steps: profiling, investable universe, sector exclusions, best-in-class ESG filters, constrained Markowitz optimization (ESG floor, risk budget, weight bounds), then pre-optimization tilt of expected returns according to your causes. The interactive simulator and detailed documentation are on the dedicated page.
reglages_inline.esg_desc_1: The ESG score ranges from 0 to 100. Instead of a fixed 40/40/20 average, the E, S, and G pillars are reweighted based on the causes you activate in your preferences. The score thus reflects what really matters to you.
reglages_inline.mapping_note: Without an active cause, we revert to the neutral 40/40/20 weighting. The more causes you activate related to a pillar, the more its weight in the composite score increases.
reglages_inline.portfolio_score_body: It is the weighted average of the composite score of each line by its weight. A default ESG floor of 70 is imposed on the optimizer; if it finds no feasible solution, the floor is relaxed and an esg_floor_relaxed flag is raised for transparency.
reglages_inline.esg_warning: ⚠️ An ESG rating remains an estimation dependent on the quality of published data. Each asset stores the score source (esg_score_source) for traceability.
reglages_inline.carbon_desc: Two indicators deliberately coexist while real data coverage reaches 100% of the portfolio:
reglages_inline.coverage_title: Low coverage? Here's what to do
reglages_inline.optimization_body: Maximization of mean-variance utility with constraints: sum of weights = 1, weights ≥ 0, floor per asset, ceiling per asset and class, risk budget (target volatility), composite ESG floor. Expected returns are tilted upstream according to your causes (single-tilt pre-optimization) — no double-tilt at the exit to avoid biasing the efficient frontier.
reglages_inline.version_body: Methodology v1.1 · E/S/G pillars weighted by causes, real carbon intensity, source traceability. Revised quarterly.

waci.label: WACI
waci.definition: Weighted Average Carbon Intensity: a portfolio's average carbon footprint, measured in tonnes of CO2e per million dollars of revenue of the companies held.

tco2e_per_musd.label: tCO2e/$M revenue
tco2e_per_musd.definition: A measure of greenhouse gas emissions relative to revenue: the lower the figure, the less a company emits per dollar earned.

carbon_intensity.label: Carbon intensity
carbon_intensity.definition: The amount of CO2 emitted relative to a unit (revenue or euro invested), allowing comparison between companies of different sizes.

data_coverage.label: Data coverage
data_coverage.definition: The share of the portfolio for which real data (rather than estimates) is available on a given indicator.

msci_acwi.label: MSCI ACWI
msci_acwi.definition: A global stock index covering thousands of companies from developed and emerging markets, often used as a market benchmark.

best_in_class.label: Best-in-class
best_in_class.definition: An approach that keeps only the highest-rated companies in each category on ESG criteria, instead of excluding an entire sector.

markowitz.label: Markowitz
markowitz.definition: A mathematical method that allocates an investment across several assets to aim for the best possible return for a given level of risk.

ter.label: TER
ter.definition: Total annual fees charged on a fund, expressed as a percentage of the amount invested (e.g. 0.20% = €2 per year for €1,000 invested).

drawdown.label: Drawdown
drawdown.definition: The largest drop observed between a peak and a trough in a portfolio's value, before it recovers.

volatility.label: Volatility
volatility.definition: The size of the swings in an investment's value over time: the higher it is, the sharper the ups and downs.

sfdr_89.label: SFDR 8/9
sfdr_89.definition: European fund classification based on environmental and social commitments: Article 9 targets an explicit sustainable objective, Article 8 promotes sustainable features without making it the main goal.

etf.label: ETF
etf.definition: An exchange-traded fund that tracks an index or basket of assets, letting you invest in many companies in a single transaction.

sector_exclusion.label: Sector exclusion
sector_exclusion.definition: The automatic, no-exception removal of an entire sector (e.g. weapons, tobacco) from the investment universe, before any scoring is done.

esg_score.label: ESG score
esg_score.definition: A composite score out of 100 assessing a company's Environmental, Social and Governance practices.

concentration.label: Concentration
concentration.definition: A measure of how much of a portfolio is held in a small number of positions: the higher it is, the more the portfolio depends on a few assets.

benchmark.label: Benchmark
benchmark.definition: A reference index or portfolio against which the performance or characteristics of an investment are compared.

why.horizon_short: You plan to invest for a short time (around {{years}} years).
why.risk_prudent: You'd rather limit ups and downs, even if growth is gentler.
why.risk_modere: You accept moderate ups and downs to aim for steady growth.
why.risk_dynamique: You accept larger ups and downs to aim for higher growth.
why.causes: The selection favours investments aligned with the values you chose.
why.exclusions: The sectors you refuse to fund have been fully excluded.

role.equity_dev: Bundles large companies from many countries — the backbone of many portfolios.
role.equity_em: Opens your portfolio to fast-growing economies.
role.thematic: Directly targets the causes you care about.
role.green_bond: Lends money to green projects — steadier than stocks.
role.social_bond: Funds projects with social value — fairly steady.
role.sov_bond: Lends to governments — cushions the portfolio's swings.
role.corporate_bond: Lends to companies — brings a more regular income.
role.reit: Diversifies your portfolio through real estate.
role.cash: Keeps part of your money aside, safely.

portfolio_glance.simulation_note: Educational simulation — Seedow informs you, you stay in control. No real transaction.
portfolio_glance.impact_basis: Computed from the ESG ratings of each investment.

portfolio_customizer.title: Adjust your portfolio
portfolio_customizer.desc: Set each line freely. Seedow shows your impact and the potential you're aiming for — you stay in control, it re-optimizes nothing on your behalf.

consequence.more_concentrated: Your portfolio is more concentrated — more of your money depends on fewer investments.
consequence.less_concentrated: Your portfolio is better spread out — your money depends on more investments.
consequence.impact_up: Your impact goes up (about +{{pts}} points out of 100).
consequence.impact_down: Your impact goes down (about −{{pts}} points out of 100).
consequence.risk_up: Your portfolio becomes a bit more sensitive to market swings.
consequence.risk_down: Your portfolio becomes a bit less sensitive to market swings.

portfolio_customizer.normalize_note: No need to land exactly on 100% — Seedow rebalances automatically on save.
portfolio_customizer.simulation_note: Educational simulation — Seedow explains, you decide. No real transaction.
portfolio_customizer.benefit_concentrated: Betting more on a few lines aims for higher upside — risk goes up too.
portfolio_customizer.benefit_balanced: Spreading across several lines aims for a steadier ride — calmer upside, gentler risk.
portfolio_customizer.need_one: Keep at least one investment to save.
portfolio_customizer.desc_v2: Boost or trim each holding in small steps. Seedow rebalances the rest and tells you, in plain words, what changes.
